TODDLER 6 · LESSON 12

Vehicles and Sounds for 2-Year-Olds

Age 2 YearsSubject Talk & ExploreClass Toddler 6Duration 3–5 minutes

Beep beep! Vroom! Choo choo! At two, vehicles are sound machines on wheels, wings and water — and this class meets twenty of them, with big cards and three quick games.

Nothing to read and nothing to test. A sound in, a sound back — a tap, a point or a giggle all count. A few playful minutes is plenty.

Start Class ↓Beep beep first. Works every time.
TODAY’S CLASS

How today’s class works.

Ten little steps, in order: a welcome from your teacher, the vehicles in three small groups, three quick games, then a hunt off screen and cards to print. Every step stands on its own.

  1. 1 Teacher welcome
  2. 2 Meet the vehicles
  3. 3 Make the sounds
  4. 4 Vehicles that work
  5. 5 Who makes this sound?
  6. 6 Boats, planes and a rocket
  7. 7 Find the vehicle
  8. 8 Where does it go?
  9. 9 Take it off screen
  10. 10 Print the cards

LEARN · VEHICLES THAT WORK

Vehicles that work.

Wheels, tracks and diggers. These ones rumble, ring and dig.

Card 1 of 6
Or simply scroll: all 6 cards are below.
PLAY · WHO MAKES THIS SOUND?

Who makes this sound?

Say the sound out loud, then let your child tap the vehicle.

Who goes choo choo?

Who goes beep beep?

Who goes vroom?

Who goes toot toot?

Who goes whirr?

Who goes ring ring?

LEARN · SKY, WATER AND A ROCKET

Boats, planes and a rocket.

Now for the flyers, floaters and zoomers — up, away and all around.

Card 1 of 8
Or simply scroll: all 8 cards are below.
PLAY · FIND THE VEHICLE

Find the vehicle.

Now by name. You say the vehicle, your child taps it.

Find the bus!

Where is the airplane?

Can you find the tractor?

Find the boat!

PLAY · WHERE DOES IT GO?

Where does it go?

One last idea: road, tracks, water or sky. You ask the question, your child picks the vehicle.

Which one goes on tracks?

Which one flies in the sky?

Which one goes on water?

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Vehicle hunt.

Look out the window or take a walk. Spot a car, bus or truck and name it together.

Try one today

  • Count the buses you see.
  • Listen for a beep.
  • Pretend to drive a car.
  • Make a train go choo choo.
  • Spot something that flies.

Keep it playful and stay close by. One spotted bus is a complete class.

PRINT THE CARDS

Print the vehicle cards.

Print the cards for vehicle hunts, matching and sound games.

View Printable Cards ↗

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Your child doesn’t need to learn every card today. Follow what catches their interest.

More from the Principal’s Office ↗

CLASS COMPLETE

Class complete!

Nice beeps, toots and choo choos together. However many rounds you played, however long it took, that was the whole class — and stopping early is allowed too.

TIPS FOR PARENTS

Tips for Parents

A toddler who answers every vehicle with vroom is doing the class exactly right. Any sound back is them talking.

Bring sounds into the body — steer a car, chug your arms like a train, rock like a boat. Movement helps words stick.

Repeats are the point. The tenth choo choo is still funny — and still teaching.

Age ranges are a guide. Go at your child’s pace.
